series.title: Path of Knowledge
series.premise: One mathematical idea per episode, built from a question to a visual proof.
series.audience: Curious adults and first-year university students.
series.visual_motif: A thin accent line becomes the graph, the proof, or the path.

episode.title: Why the derivative of x² is 2x
episode.thesis: The derivative is the limit of secant slopes, and that limit turns the geometry of x² into the algebra of 2x.
episode.question: Why does the slope of x² at x equal 2x, rather than something that still depends on h?
episode.audience: First-year calculus students who know functions and slopes but are shaky on limits.
goals: Explain the derivative as a limit of secant slopes.
Derive 2x for x² from the limit definition.
Recognize the cancellation step as the crux.
key_points: A secant slope is an average rate.
The limit turns average into instantaneous.
The h cancels before h reaches zero.
misconceptions: The derivative is just a formula to memorize.
Setting h to zero is allowed before cancelling.
The tangent is the secant at a single point.
visuals: Secant line closing onto a tangent as h shrinks.
The rise/run triangle with h and f(x+h)-f(x) labeled.
The graph of x² with the tangent slope at x = 1.
episode.next_teaser: What happens when the function is not a parabola?

notation: Use f'(x) for the derivative; do not mix Leibniz and Newton notation in one derivation.
Use \mathbb{R} for the domain unless a restriction is stated.
accuracy.conventions: Angles in radians. Decimal point, not comma.
sources: Stewart, Calculus, chapter 2 (for the limit definition)
claims_to_verify: The cancellation is valid for h ≠ 0.
